questions.question: Which word means 'continuing to live, especially in very hard conditions'?
questions.explanation: Survival means staying alive even when things are difficult, like animals surviving a long dry season.

questions.question: Amina is very proud ___ her science project. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Some adjectives carry their own preposition — we are always proud OF something we did well.

questions.question: The two teams had to ___ to finish the school mural before Friday. Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: To cooperate means to work together with others to reach a goal — just what two teams sharing one mural must do.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: Everyone in my class have a favourite book. | Everyone in my class are reading fans. | Everyone in my class enjoy reading. | Everyone in my class enjoys reading.
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone in my class enjoys reading.
questions.explanation: Everyone sounds like many people, but it takes a singular verb — everyone enjoys, everyone has.

questions.question: Which word names a set of rules that explains how a country or organisation works?
questions.explanation: A constitution is the big rule book of a country or organisation — it explains how everything should work.

questions.question: Of the three stories we read, this one is the ___. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Good is an irregular adjective: good, better, best. When we compare three or more things, we use best.

questions.question: Ali packed his bag in a ___ way and forgot his lunch. Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: Hasty means doing something too quickly without thinking carefully — that is how lunches get forgotten!

questions.question: Which sentence uses a relative clause correctly?
questions.options: The girl which won the race is my cousin. | The girl who won the race is my cousin. | The girl what won the race is my cousin. | The girl she won the race is my cousin.
questions.correctAnswer: The girl who won the race is my cousin.
questions.explanation: We use who for people in a defining relative clause: the girl who won the race.

questions.question: Which sentence gives an instruction, the way a recipe does?
questions.options: She mixes the flour and water in a bowl. | I mixed the flour and water in a bowl. | Mix the flour and water in a bowl. | We might mix the flour and water in a bowl.
questions.correctAnswer: Mix the flour and water in a bowl.
questions.explanation: Instructions start with an imperative verb — a command word like mix, pour or stir.

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ___. Which word completes this zero conditional sentence?
questions.explanation: The zero conditional tells us what always happens: if you heat ice, it melts — every single time.

questions.question: We wanted to play outside, ___ it started to rain. Which conjunction fits best?
questions.explanation: But joins two ideas that pull in different directions — we wanted to play, and the rain got in the way.

questions.question: An ___ visitor knocked on the door — nobody knew he was coming. Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: Unexpected describes something that happens suddenly, without anyone planning it or knowing it would come.

questions.question: Which of these sentences is an OPINION?
questions.options: Football is the most exciting sport in the world. | Many countries have national football teams. | A football match is played in two halves. | A football team has eleven players on the pitch.
questions.correctAnswer: Football is the most exciting sport in the world.
questions.explanation: An opinion tells us what someone thinks or feels. 'Most exciting' cannot be proved — it is a feeling, not a fact.

questions.question: Which word describes the countryside, far away from towns and cities?
questions.explanation: Rural places are in the countryside — think of farms, fields and quiet villages.

questions.question: Layla has lived in Hargeisa ___ 2020. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: With the present perfect, since points to when something started (since 2020), and for measures how long (for four years).

questions.question: Her quick answers in the quiz showed her ___. Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: Intelligence is the ability to learn, understand and think about things — quick quiz answers show it off nicely.

questions.question: Which word is a compound noun — two words joined to make one new thing?
questions.explanation: Toothbrush joins tooth + brush into one new noun. That is exactly what a compound noun is.

questions.question: Read this: 'The astronauts checked their equipment twice, because in space even a small mistake can become a big problem.' Why did the astronauts check twice?
questions.options: Because in space a small mistake can grow into a big problem | Because they had lost some of their equipment | Because they had extra time before the launch | Because their commander ordered them to check
questions.correctAnswer: Because in space a small mistake can grow into a big problem
questions.explanation: The word 'because' hands us the reason: in space, small mistakes can become big problems, so careful checking matters.

questions.question: Which phrase puts the adjectives in the correct order?
questions.options: a beautiful old wooden box | an old wooden beautiful box | a wooden beautiful old box | a beautiful wooden old box
questions.explanation: Adjectives usually line up as opinion, then age, then material: beautiful (opinion), old (age), wooden (material).

questions.question: Your friend says a film is brilliant, but you disagree. Which reply is polite?
questions.options: Nobody cares what you think about films. | I see your point, but I think the book is better. | That is a silly thing to say. | You are wrong, so stop talking about it.
questions.correctAnswer: I see your point, but I think the book is better.
questions.explanation: Polite disagreement starts by respecting the other person's idea — 'I see your point' — before sharing your own.

questions.question: An elephant is ___ than a cat. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: To compare two things with a short adjective, we add -er: big becomes bigger.

questions.question: Which meal do we eat in the morning to start the day?
questions.explanation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day — it gives our bodies energy for the morning.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: There are a shop on my street. | There are three shops on my street. | There is three shops on my street. | There be three shops on my street.
questions.correctAnswer: There are three shops on my street.
questions.explanation: We use 'there are' with plural nouns like three shops, and 'there is' with just one thing.

questions.question: Yesterday we ___ to the park after school. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Yesterday tells us the action is finished, so we need the past simple: go becomes went.

questions.question: Sara has ___ a camel twice in her life. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: For life experiences we use the present perfect: has + ridden. Sara has ridden a camel twice — how exciting!

questions.question: Students ___ wear a helmet when they cycle to school. Which words complete the sentence?
questions.options: having to | have to | has to | had have to
questions.explanation: We use 'have to' for rules and obligations. Students is plural, so it takes have to, not has to.

questions.question: Next week, Omar is ___ visit his grandmother. Which words complete the sentence?
questions.options: go to | gone to | going to | goes to
questions.explanation: For plans we have already decided, we use 'is going to': Omar is going to visit his grandmother next week.

questions.question: Which word names the loud sound you hear in the sky during a storm?
questions.explanation: Thunder is the big rumbling sound that follows lightning in a storm.

questions.question: Which word begins with the same sound as 'sun'?
questions.explanation: Sun and sock both start with the /s/ sound — sss, like a little snake.

questions.question: What do we call your mother’s mother?
questions.explanation: Your mother’s mother is your grandmother — the grandma of the family.

questions.question: Which day comes right after Monday?
questions.explanation: The days of the week go Monday, then Tuesday — one after the other, all week long.

questions.question: One box, two ___. Which word completes the phrase?
questions.explanation: Words that end in x add -es to become plural: one box, two boxes.

questions.question: Hassan ___ up at seven o’clock every morning. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: For things that happen every day, we use the present simple. With he or she, the verb takes -s: Hassan wakes.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.options: The cat sleeps little warm on the mat. | Little the cat on sleeps the warm mat. | The cat little sleeps on the mat warm. | The little cat sleeps on the warm mat.
questions.correctAnswer: The little cat sleeps on the warm mat.
questions.explanation: Describing words come before the noun they describe: the little cat, the warm mat.
